what: MongoDB makes a database built around documents rather than rows and columns, which developers often find faster to build with. Most revenue now comes from Atlas, its managed cloud version.
customers: Software developers and companies of all sizes building applications, from startups to large enterprises.
money: the managed cloud database service, billed by consumption
moat: Once an application's data model is built around it, moving to another database means rewriting the application, so adoption at the developer level turns into long-term revenue.
risks: It still makes an operating loss because of large stock-based compensation
Consumption pricing means revenue falls when customers optimise spending
Cloud providers offer competing document databases
The shares trade at a high multiple of revenue
opportunities: Revenue grew about 23% last year and about 24% a year over three years
Cash of about $2.4 billion against almost no debt
Analysts see about 38% upside from current levels
watch: Atlas revenue growth and net ARR expansion.
